name: Product Requirements Discovery
objective: Turn a rough idea or a discovered opportunity into a reviewable, implementation-ready specification by interviewing the idea owner about the problem, users, functionality, workflows, business rules, constraints, integrations, security, data, technical preferences and edge cases.

coverageAreas.name: Product overview and problem
coverageAreas.description: What problem, for whom, why now.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Problem statement with who has it and what happens if unsolved.

coverageAreas.name: Target users and roles
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each role has a goal and a first action.

coverageAreas.name: User stories
coverageAreas.description: What each role does with the product.

coverageAreas.name: Functional requirements
coverageAreas.description: Capabilities, each tagged mvp or future.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Every requirement has an id, a tag and at least one acceptance criterion.

coverageAreas.name: Business rules
coverageAreas.description: Rules and edge cases that govern behavior.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Rules exist for every decision point in the flows.

coverageAreas.name: Technical requirements
coverageAreas.description: Team skills, backend, frontend, database, hosting, auth, architecture. One decision per question, each with a default.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each decision is made or its default accepted.

coverageAreas.name: Data requirements
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Entities and relationships are listed with retention.

coverageAreas.name: Integrations
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each integration has direction, data and auth.

coverageAreas.name: Security and privacy
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Roles, data classes and compliance needs are known.

coverageAreas.name: Non-functional requirements
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Targets are numbers or explicitly deferred.

coverageAreas.name: Administrative surface
coverageAreas.description: What operators and admins need to configure and see. Enumerate it explicitly.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: The admin surface is listed and each item is mvp or future.

coverageAreas.name: MVP scope
coverageAreas.description: The smallest version that solves the core problem.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Owner has confirmed the mvp set and challenged items were resolved.

coverageAreas.name: Future scope
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Deferred items are listed with the reason.

coverageAreas.name: Implementation phases
coverageAreas.description: Ordered, independently testable phases for a developer or coding agent.
coverageAreas.doneWhen: Each phase has tasks, dependencies and acceptance.

aiInstructions: Estimate the user's technical level from the first answers and adapt: technical users get architecture, API and data questions; nontechnical users get behavior questions and plain-language recommendations for technical decisions. Ask one decision per question when the build impact is high; never bundle stack decisions. Never default a technology choice before asking what the team knows. Every question states why it matters and offers a default the user can accept in one word. Enumerate administrative surfaces explicitly and ask what is missing. Challenge MVP items that are not needed to solve the core problem. Run an issues pass every five turns: look for ambiguity, contradictions, missing decisions and unnecessary complexity, and raise them one at a time.
